description.text: AMG is a strategic partner to leading independent investment firms globally. Our strategy is to generate long-term value by investing in high-quality independent partner-owned firms, which we refer to as “Affiliates,” through a proven partnership approach, and allocating resources across our unique opportunity set to the areas of highest growth and return. We believe that high-quality, partner-owned firms have fundamental competitive advantages in meeting client objectives. With their entrepreneurial, investment-centric cultures, and deep alignment of interests with clients through direct equity ownership by firm principals, independent firms have an ownership mindset, a long-term orientation to building their firms, and the ability to act nimbly to capitalize on market movements, enabling them to offer unique return streams to the marketplace. AMG’s distinctive partnership approach magnifies the existing advantages of our independent Affiliates and actively supports their ongoing independence and ownership culture. Our innovative model enables each Affiliate’s management team to retain autonomy and significant equity ownership in their firm, while they leverage our strategic capabilities and insight, including access to growth capital, product strategy and distribution through our capital formation capabilities, succession planning, and strategic advisory, to expand their reach, diversify their businesses, and enhance their long-term success.

about.description_short: AMG (NYSE: AMG) is a strategic partner to leading independent investment management firms globally. AMG's strategy is to generate long-term value by investing in high-quality independent partner-owned firms, through a proven partnership approach, and allocating resources across AMG's unique opportunity set to the areas of highest growth and return. Through its distinctive approach, AMG magnifies its Affiliates' existing advantages and actively supports their independence and ownership culture. As of June 30, 2026, AMG's aggregate assets under management were approximately $942 billion across a diverse range of private markets, liquid alternative, and differentiated long-only investment strategies.

analysis_md:
# AMG — Affiliated Managers Group, Inc.
Engine 5.5 run, 2026-10-19. Market cap $12.708B at $385.10 (nasdaq_quote_api) — in scope under $40B. SIC 6282 Investment Advice.

All figures below are copied from key_numbers.md, dcf_numbers.json, ttm.json, financials_history.csv or the computed enrichment outputs — none are recomputed.

## What it is
A multi-affiliate asset manager: AMG holds partnership stakes (typically majority economic interests) in ~40 independent boutique managers ("Affiliates") running 500+ strategies across private markets, liquid alternatives, multi-asset and long-only equities, and takes its share of their fee earnings while leaving investment autonomy in place. Since ~2019 it has pivoted the mix toward alternatives — now ~60% of earnings — funded by its recurring after-tax cash flow, affiliate divestitures, and aggressive buybacks. AUM was a record $942.4B at Q2 2026 (search: Zacks Q2 2026 report — revenue $640.7M, +29.9% YoY; net client inflows $12.9B in the quarter, led by alternatives; economic EPS $8.29, +58.3% YoY).

## Owner's earnings
**FY2025 (10-K via EDGAR, from financials_history.csv):** revenue $2,074,400,000; operating cash flow $973,200,000; capex $6,100,000 (PaymentsToAcquirePropertyPlantAndEquipment — trivially small, asset-light); SBC $59,200,000 (AllocatedShareBasedCompensationExpense tag).
- **Conservative owner's earnings FY2025: $907,900,000 = $27.51/share** (latest FY OE/share). The maintenance definition is not computed in the outputs (D&A is not tagged), so no second figure is quoted.
- OE/share history (conservative): FY2023 $17.77, FY2024 $22.63, FY2025 $27.51. OE positive 5 of the last 5 fiscal years.
- Net debt $2,105,300,000 (total debt $2,691,300,000 LongTermDebt less cash $586,000,000); net debt is 2.82x normalized OE (dcf_numbers.json diagnostics). Shares: latest diluted 33,000,000; cover-page outstanding 25,859,933 at 2026-08-05 — the gap is the junior convertible / adjusted-diluted basis that was retired in January 2026 (search: Q4 2025 release — the refinancing "removed the associated share count dilution"), plus continued buybacks ($700M repurchased in FY2025; ~$375M in H1 2026, full-year guide ~$600M).
- Consolidation caveat (method limit): consolidated OCF carries 100% of consolidated Affiliates' cash flow while noncontrolling holders own a share of several Affiliates, so consolidated OE overstates what belongs to common shareholders to an unquantified degree. This is one reason the conservative (median) base and a low confidence grade are used.

**Base used = median of the last 3 FY OE/share: $22.63/share** (base_source: median_of_last_3_fy_oe_per_share).

**TTM rejected — with the legs quoted.** ttm.py through Q2 2026 gives: OCF FY $973,200,000 − prior YTD $439,700,000 + current YTD $538,300,000 = TTM $1,071,800,000; capex TTM $6,900,000; shares (current-YTD diluted) 27,300,000 — but the SBC leg is broken: FY $59,200,000 (AllocatedShareBasedCompensationExpense) − prior YTD $92,300,000 (ShareBasedCompensation) + current YTD $17,100,000 (AllocatedShareBasedCompensationExpense) = **TTM SBC −$16,000,000**, a negative stock-comp figure produced by mixing two tags that measure different scopes (in FY2019–FY2024 the Share tag ran roughly 2x the Allocated tag — $111,600,000 vs $52,000,000 in FY2024 — and the engine used the Share tag; in FY2025 only the Allocated figure is filed for the full year, while the H1 2025 10-Q filed the Share figure). A negative SBC adds $16M to TTM OE instead of subtracting a real cost and inflates the TTM base to $39.59/share; the quarterly-summed statements output gives yet a third SBC TTM figure ($98,300,000). No TTM base built on these legs is quotable, so the median base is used and the TTM is not pinned. The direction of the error matters: using the TTM figure would have flattered the tier.

## Moat: 5/10 — moderate/narrow
- FOR: multi-affiliate diversification (~40 Affiliates, 500+ strategies) stabilizes earnings across cycles; alternatives mix (private markets + liquid alternatives, ~60% of earnings) carries longer lock-ups and higher fees, with record inflows (Q2 2026 AUM $942.4B, +22.2% YoY); a three-decade founder-trust reputation plus flexible succession/structuring in the market for affiliate partnerships; global distribution the boutiques cannot build alone; permanent public capital; adjusted diluted share count down ~38% since Q2 2021 on disciplined buybacks.
- AGAINST: end-client switching costs are low — assets follow performance, fees and consultants; secular fee pressure from passive in traditional long-only; key-person/culture risk at semi-autonomous Affiliates; full market beta in AUM and performance fees; competition for quality alternative affiliates bids up the price of growth.
- Evidence check (WORKER_SPEC step 5): the computed roic_proxy series in fundamentals.json exists only for early years (19.3% in FY2016); operating income is not tagged in companyfacts after FY2018, so no recent ROIC or gross-margin series is available in the computed outputs — a trailing ROE of 21.94% is reported in search results (Zacks), but on a buyback-shrunk equity base that overstates franchise returns. A 5 sits on the qualitative pillars above; the evidence does not support 7+.
- A 5 gives CAP = 8.5 years: growth holds 2 years, then converges linearly to the 2.5% terminal rate over 8.5 years, 15-year projection.

## DCF — final run (2026-10-19)
Growth sanity check: the engine blend is 6.05%, built from revenue CAGR 5y +0.46%, revenue CAGR 3y −3.79%, latest revenue YoY +1.64% (the flat FY2023–FY2025 consolidated revenue of ~$2.04–2.07B) and OE/share CAGR 2y +24.42% (largely buyback arithmetic), with a +5pp share-count adjustment (share count −12.34%/yr). The recent prints are stronger than the FY window: TTM revenue $2,270,200,000, +11.80% YoY (fundamentals.json), and Q2 2026 revenue +29.9% YoY — partly new-Affiliate consolidation, not pure organic growth. Scenario starts are therefore set modestly above the blend (offsets −0.10 / −0.03 / +0.02 / +0.07 / +0.12 vs g_base) to −3.95 / +3.05 / **+8.05** / +13.05 / +18.05%: the base start sits between the blend and the TTM revenue print, and even the super-bull start (18.05%) is below the latest quarterly revenue print (+29.9%) because that print includes acquired AUM. Probabilities 10/25/30/25/10; OE multipliers 0.75/0.90/1.00/1.10/1.25. Price $385.10.

| Scenario | Prob | Growth start | OE mult | Story | IV@15 | IRR |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Super bear | 10% | −3.95% | 0.75 | Market drawdown cuts AUM and performance fees; traditional outflows dominate | $106.30 | 5.72% |
| Bear | 25% | +3.05% | 0.90 | Alternatives inflows cool; flat markets; fee pressure | $170.91 | 8.07% |
| Base | 30% | +8.05% | 1.00 | Alternatives momentum decays to mid-single-digit AUM growth plus buybacks | $233.64 | 10.27% |
| Bull | 25% | +13.05% | 1.10 | Alternatives stay ~60%+ of earnings with sustained double-digit inflows | $315.63 | 12.93% |
| Super bull | 10% | +18.05% | 1.25 | Record-AUM trajectory compounds; EPS growth near management's long-term claims | $439.55 | 16.52% |

- **Probability-weighted: IV@15% $246.31 (upside vs price −36.0%), IV@20% $171.34, IV@25% $130.41, weighted IRR 10.72%, base-case IRR 10.27%**
- **Tier by numbers: C.** Diagnostics (dcf_numbers.json): OE yield 5.88%, terminal value 19.6% of IV@15%, scenario spread 4.14x, net debt 2.82x normalized OE, 9.6 months since FY end.
- Hurdle-clearing price: the stock clears the 15% hurdle only at or below the weighted IV@15% of $246.31 — roughly 36% below the current price.

## Flags — every fragility flag resolved
- **STALE_FY** (latest FY ended 9.6 months ago): ttm.py was run and its legs are quoted above; the TTM base was rejected because its SBC leg is a tag-mixing artifact (−$16,000,000), so the median FY base is used instead. The Q2 2026 prints (revenue +29.9% YoY, record AUM) are reflected in the scenario growth starts rather than in a corrupted base.
- **BUYBACK_TAILWIND** (share count shrinking 12.34%/yr): real and documented — ~$700M repurchased in FY2025, ~$375M in H1 2026, adjusted diluted count down ~38% since Q2 2021. Already credited via the +5pp growth adjustment in the blend; not double-counted in the verdict. Note part of the latest diluted-count drop is the January 2026 junior convertible retirement, a one-off capital-structure cleanup, not a repeatable buyback pace.
- **NI_OCF_DIVERGENCE** (2024: net income $511,600,000 vs OCF $932,100,000, >40% apart): partly explained by the computed addbacks — SBC $111,600,000 and deferred income taxes $60,600,000 (statements.json cash-flow lines for FY2024); the balance is non-cash Affiliate equity-allocation/amortization and equity-method distribution timing that the computed outputs do not tag separately. No single tax-deposit or impairment one-off was found. The 3-year median base smooths any single year's divergence, and the OCF-based OE series is the one used throughout.
- **SECTOR_MODEL_MISMATCH** (Finance): confidence graded low, as required. AMG is an asset manager, not a float-funded insurer or a deposit-funded bank — consolidated OCF is its Affiliates' fee cash flow, not policyholder or depositor money — so the insurer-float tier notch does not apply; the model risk here is the NCI consolidation caveat above and AUM market beta, handled via the median base and low confidence.
- **WIDE_SCENARIO_SPREAD** (super-bull IV 4.14x super-bear IV): real — outcomes hinge on market levels and alternatives fundraising. Confidence is low (also capped by the sector misfit), and the verdict is sized to the conservative end.
- **TIER_BAND** (bear tier D at 8.07% vs bull tier C at 12.93%): the verdict spans tiers; any position should be sized to the bear end. Even the bull case does not reach the 15% hurdle at this price.

## My thoughts / overlay
- The honest headline is the method range: on the filed median base the name is a C (10.72% weighted); on the rejected TTM base ($39.59/share) the same scenarios would print materially higher — that gap is an SBC-tag artifact, not economics, and is exactly why the TTM was not used.
- The business is genuinely inflecting — alternatives inflows, record AUM, +29.9% Q2 revenue — but the price ($385.10, near the 52-week high of $395 per search results) already capitalizes it: even the bull scenario (12.93% IRR) fails the 15% hurdle, and only the super bull clears it.
- Balance sheet is manageable (net debt 2.82x normalized OE, investment-grade A3/BBB+ per search results) and capital return is heavy, but buybacks at ~17x the median base OE/share are far less accretive than they were at the $173 average repurchase price of the last five years (search: AMG Q2 2026 investor overview).

## Final verdict
- **Final tier: C** (weighted IRR 10.72%; bear D 8.07%, bull C 12.93% — sized to the bear end)
- Confidence: **Low** (sector model misfit, wide scenario spread, TTM SBC data conflict, NCI consolidation caveat)
- One-liner: Diversified multi-affiliate asset manager pivoting to alternatives, moat 5/10 — at $385.10 it does not clear 15% (weighted IRR 10.7%, IV@15 $246.31; clears 15% only below ~$246), and the finance-sector model fit is poor, so confidence is low.
